raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

While collecting baseline numbers for #58241 (block FP8 on SM89), I found that `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_block_fp8_gemm.py` no longer runs on main.

The script has drifted from the current FP8 kernel API in three places:

- `init_fp8_linear_kernel` now requires `input_dtype` and `weight_shape`, which the script does not pass.
- The block-scaled kernels expose `apply_weights(layer, x)`; the script still calls `apply(...)`, which no longer exists.
- `use_cutlass` was accepted but never used, so the "triton" and "cutlass" providers both ran whichever kernel the selector picked, rather than the kernel in their name.

This PR builds a small layer with `weight` / `weight_scale_inv` (the same names `Fp8LinearMethod` registers), runs `process_weights_after_loading` so each kernel sees the weights it would see in a real model, and passes `force_kernel` so each provider benchmarks the kernel it names. It also asserts that the kernel it got is the one it forced, since `force_kernel` falls back to another kernel when the forced one can't be used.

I checked that no open PR touches this file.

AI assistance was used to read through the kernel API. I wrote the fix, tested it end to end on an L4 and an H100, and reviewed every line.

## Test Plan

NVIDIA L4 (SM89), torch 2.13.0+cu132, vLLM main @ 741edeebe (precompiled install), and NVIDIA H100 PCIe (SM90), torch 2.13.0+cu130 (precompiled install of this branch):

```bash
uv pip install matplotlib pandas   # required by triton.testing.perf_report; not new to this PR
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_block_fp8_gemm.py
```

`pre-commit run` passes (ruff, mypy, typos).

## Test Result

**Before (main):**

```
TypeError: init_fp8_linear_kernel() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'input_dtype' and 'weight_shape'
```

**After (this PR):** the script runs through all 11 DeepSeek-V3 shapes and prints `Benchmark finished!`. Two of the shapes on the L4 (TFLOP/s, higher is better):

**N=2112, K=7168**

| M | torch-bf16 | w8a8-block-fp8-triton |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.83 | 0.36 |
| 16 | 10.8 | 6.5 |
| 64 | 41.3 | 24.3 |
| 128 | 56.3 | 44.4 |
| 256 | 51.5 | 57.1 |
| 1024 | 57.6 | 65.1 |
| 4096 | 56.0 | 63.4 |
| 16384 | 55.4 | 63.8 |

**N=7168, K=2048**

| M | torch-bf16 | w8a8-block-fp8-triton |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.85 | 0.57 |
| 16 | 15.1 | 16.8 |
| 64 | 34.2 | 63.5 |
| 128 | 52.8 | 84.9 |
| 256 | 61.5 | 84.9 |
| 1024 | 63.8 | 82.6 |
| 4096 | 58.6 | 71.6 |
| 16384 | 54.1 | 71.7 |

On SM89 only the bf16 and Triton providers appear, because CUTLASS block FP8 is not yet supported there (#58241). Every shape also logs `Config file not found ... device_name=NVIDIA_L4`, so the Triton numbers use default configs.

**H100 PCIe (SM90):** the script runs all 11 shapes with all three providers (`torch-bf16`, `w8a8-block-fp8-triton`, `w8a8-block-fp8-cutlass`) and prints `Benchmark finished!`. Each provider now asserts that the forced kernel is the one being benchmarked. Numbers are in the comment below.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

 from vllm.benchmarks.lib.utils import default_vllm_config
 from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear import (
+    CutlassFp8BlockScaledMMKernel,
+    TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel,
     init_fp8_linear_kernel,
 )
 from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import (
@@ -43,7 +45,7 @@
 
 
 @default_vllm_config()
-def build_w8a8_block_fp8_runner(M, N, K, block_size, device, use_cutlass):
+def build_w8a8_block_fp8_runner(M, N, K, block_size, device, kernel_type):
     """Build runner function for w8a8 block fp8 matmul."""
     factor_for_scale = 1e-2
 
@@ -78,18 +80,24 @@ def build_w8a8_block_fp8_runner(M, N, K, block_size, device, use_cutlass):
         activation_quant_key=create_fp8_quant_key(
             static=False, group_shape=act_quant_group_shape
         ),
-        out_dtype=torch.get_default_dtype(),
+        input_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        out_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        weight_shape=(N, K),
+        force_kernel=kernel_type,
         module_name="build_w8a8_block_fp8_runner",
     )
 
+    assert type(linear_op) is kernel_type, (
+        f"Requested {kernel_type.__name__}, got {type(linear_op).__name__}"
+    )
+
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(B, requires_grad=False)
+    layer.weight_scale_inv = torch.nn.Parameter(Bs, requires_grad=False)
+    linear_op.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+
     def run():
-        return linear_op.apply(
-            input=A_ref,
-            weight=B,
-            weight_scale=Bs,
-            input_scale=None,
-            bias=None,
-        )
+        return linear_op.apply_weights(layer, A_ref)
 
     return run

         ms, min_ms, max_ms = vllm_triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(
